newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi up on acquisition rumours.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi up on acquisition rumours.

text.p: Banque Audi rose 4.8 percent to a new high on Monday on rumours that it was hunting for a local bank to buy after last week losing the race to acquire Credit Libanais.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce continued its upward surge and Solidere A and B also rose in heavy demand.
The LIBX bank index rose 2.4 percent to 175.91. The LISPI general index climbed 0.86 percent to 91.47 and the BLOM general index rose 1.14 percent to 979.67.
Total market turnover rose to 411,136 shares from 210,378 on Friday for a value of $4,366,352 against $3,335,861.

Market rumours said Banque Audi, which jumped to $27.5 from $26.25, was looking for an acquisition to increase its market share after losing out last week to billionaire Saudi Sheikh Khalid bin Mahfouz who bought Credit Libanais from the central bank for $163 million.

Market sources said Banque Audi had wanted to acquire Credit Libanais for its 3.43 percent market share. It believed that taking over a bank was the cheapest way of increasing its own market share, the sources said.
Solidere A and B rose in heavy demand amid a marked scarcity of supply on the B shares. A shares rose to $11 from $10.875 and B shares rose to $11.375 from $11.25.
Brokers said Solidere shares were a bargain at their present prices.
"Frankly, all the shares are fairly valued but Solidere is really undervalued. It is really a catch," a broker who asked not to be identified said.
Demand for A shares was 268,932 against a supply of 161,966 on the first fixing. Demand for B shares was 185,428 against a supply of 4,050 -- all of which were traded on the first fixing.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to a record $20.5 from $20. "BLC is on the right path," a broker said.
Bank of Beirut was unchanged at $4.375 on a turnover of 45,000 shares and a block of 50,000 traded on the bourse at $4.375.
The exchange said 15,000 BLC shares were traded in a block off the floor on July 6 at $20.25.
There was no trade in the four industrial firms, Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blanc, Eternit and Uniceramic.
